conventions.step: one step per executed instruction line; `block`/`loop`/`if`/`br*`/`return`/`call` count, `else`/`end` do not; a `call` takes two steps (enter: args popped; return: result pushed). Spec checks happen after the step they are attached to.
conventions.values: i32 shown as signed decimal; predicates read them as mathematical integers (signed) unless written u(x)
conventions.frame: {s: step, fn, ln: line (1-based, in the program listing, which is the same for buggy variants because deleted lines are blanked, not removed), op, stack (after the step, bottom first), loc: locals incl. ghost, checks: spec checks evaluated at this step}
conventions.hash_frame_extra: used: global $used; M: ghost map as [key, value] pairs; slots: 8 x [state, key, value] (0 EMPTY, 1 FULL, 2 TOMB); R: truth of each clause of the representation invariant at that instant (only REQUIRED at function boundaries; transient falsity mid-operation is normal)
conventions.status: none = no obligation beyond Wasm typing; auto = discharged from the refined stack + path condition by linear/bit-vector reasoning; inv = needs the loop invariant or the representation invariant R; lemma = also needs a nonlinear, counting, or definitional lemma; fails = the obligation that a seeded bug breaks

bugs.title: signed comparison of a product that may exceed 2^31-1
bugs.runtime: n = 2147483647: never terminates (no i32 is signed-greater than INT_MAX). n = 2147395600 (smallest failing input): returns 289398 after ~4.3M steps. The real run reaches the bad loop-head state (r = 46340) only at step 695,104, far past Codillon's 100k-step log, so the trace below is the counterexample-to-induction: start at a loop head satisfying the invariant and run one iteration (add 695,100 to each step number to get the real-run step).

static_failure.why: signed reading of the line-15 product is faithful only if (r+1)^2 <= 2^31-1, i.e. r <= 46339; the invariant r*r <= n only gives r <= 46340. At r = 46340 the product 2147488281 wraps to -2147479015

bugs.trace_note: counterexample-to-induction: one loop iteration from the loop-head state n = 2147483647, r = 46340 (which satisfies the invariant). Real-run step = s + 695100.

(@define h(k) = k & 7, at(k, d) = (h(k) + d) & 7, dist(k, s) = (s - h(k)) & 7)
(@define R0 = forall s in 0..7. st(s) in {EMPTY, FULL, TOMB})
(@define R1 = forall s. st(s) == FULL ==> key(s) in M && M[key(s)] == val(s))
(@define R2 = forall k in M. #{s | st(s) == FULL && key(s) == k} == 1)
(@define R3 = forall s. st(s) == FULL ==> forall d <= dist(key(s), s). st(at(key(s), d)) != EMPTY)
(@define R4 = #{s | st(s) == FULL} == |M| && used == #{s | st(s) != EMPTY} && used < CAP)
(@define R = R0 && R1 && R2 && R3 && R4)
(@invariant 0 <= j && j <= used && i == at(k, j))
(@invariant forall d < j. st(at(k, d)) == TOMB || (st(at(k, d)) == FULL && key(at(k, d)) != k))
(@invariant !(k in M) && 0 <= j && j <= used && i == at(k, j))
(@invariant forall d < j. st(at(k, d)) != EMPTY)

bugs.title: (a) probe index not wrapped
observed_results: trap: out of bounds memory access
bugs.runtime: insert(15, 150) traps "out of bounds memory access" at line 142 (address 65536 = BASE + 12*8).

static_failure.why: after line 146 i == at(k, j) + 1, which is 8 when at(k, j) == 7. The back-edge invariant i == at(k, j+1) (line 136) fails first

bugs.R_violation: none: the trap fires before any write. With BASE = 0 instead of 65440 there would be no trap: "slot 8" (bytes 96..107) reads as EMPTY, the entry is written outside the table, and R2 (ii) fails because 15 is in M but in no FULL slot

bugs.title: (b) lookup treats TOMBSTONE as EMPTY
bugs.edit: line 38: `i32.lt_u` (state < FULL, i.e. EMPTY) -> `i32.ne` (state != FULL, i.e. EMPTY or TOMB)
bugs.runtime: lookup(11, -1) returns -1 (expected 110). No trap. Cascade: a later insert(11, 111) sees "absent" and writes a second FULL slot for 11 (slot 5), now breaking R2 (ii).

static_failure.why: the path condition at the early return is now st(i) in {EMPTY, TOMB}; R3 (iii) only promises no EMPTY on a key's probe path, so a TOMB there says nothing about k

bugs.R_violation: R stays TRUE at every step (delete correctly writes TOMB). What breaks is the stronger invariant the buggy lookup silently relies on, iii_strong = "no non-FULL slot on any key's probe path". It becomes false at step 217 (delete's i32.store, line 100), when slot 3 on key 11's path turns TOMB. The first obligation to fail at runtime is $find's postcondition, at step 241 (find returns -1 to lookup)

static_failure.why: writing EMPTY into slot 3 places an EMPTY on key 11's path h(11)=3 .. 4

bugs.R_violation: R3 (iii) and R4 (iv: used == #non-EMPTY) become false at step 217 (line 100, the store)
